In mathematics, more specifically in [[topology]], the '''equivariant stable homotopy theory''' is a subfield of [[equivariant topology]] that studies a [[spectrum (topology)|spectrum]] with [[Group action (mathematics)|group action]] instead of a space with group action, as in [[stable homotopy theory]]. The field has become more active recently because of its connection to [[algebraic K-theory]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.birs.ca/workshops/2012/12w5116/report12w5116.pdf |format=PDF |title=Algebraic K-Theory and Equivariant Homotopy Theory |publisher=Birs.ca |accessdate=2015-03-11}}</ref>
